t: Founded by Lê Lợi, who ended twenty years of Ming occupation in 1428, it was Vietnam's longest-reigning dynasty.
Under Lê Thánh Tông (1460–1497) it became a Confucian bureaucratic state and conquered the Cham capital Vijaya in 1471.
From the 1530s the emperors were figureheads while the Trịnh lords ruled the north and the Nguyễn lords the south.
dyk: The names of Lê-era doctoral graduates were carved on stone stelae resting on turtles at Hanoi's Temple of Literature from 1484; dozens of these stelae still stand there.
ev: Lê Lợi launches his revolt against Ming rule at Lam Sơn
Lê Lợi takes the throne as Lê Thái Tổ at Thăng Long
Lê Thánh Tông captures Vijaya, the capital of Champa
Mạc Đăng Dung seizes the throne and founds the Mạc dynasty
Lê and Trịnh forces retake Thăng Long from the Mạc
War between the Trịnh and Nguyễn lords begins; a truce follows in 1672
The Tây Sơn overthrow the Trịnh lords
Quang Trung defeats the Qing at Đống Đa; Lê Chiêu Thống flees to China
